I read the code. Right now the app reads `sailings.csv` (the nightly export from the ferry office) and renders it into `timetable.html`. Nothing in that file marks a sailing as cancelled. There is no warning code either. So the hard part is not the warning on the page. The hard part is where the cancellation information comes from.

That matters because of timing. The export runs once each night. Most cancellations happen on the day, for example because of weather or a fault. A cancellation that only reaches the site with the next night's export would come too late to warn anyone.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The site is a read-only view of a once-a-night snapshot. A warning feature adds data that changes during the day, and the current design has no path for that.
- The answer to "who knows first, and how do they tell the system" decides most of the build: a CSV column, an admin form, or a feed from another system.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

When the ferry office cancels a sailing today, who finds out first, and how do they tell people now?
